title: Definitely Not A Secret
story: Security found a file on Bob's desktop called definitely_not_a_secret.txt.
Bob insists it is not a secret.
Bob also insists it is 'military-grade encrypted'.
Both of these cannot be true. Possibly neither.
objective: Decode the deploy key hidden in Bob's not-a-secret file.

/home/bob/desktop/definitely_not_a_secre: This file is definitely not a secret.
If it were a secret, it would be encrypted.
/home/bob/desktop/encryption_notes.txt: - the '=' at the end means it's extra secure
- to decrypt you would need the 'base64 -d' command
which hackers do not know about
files./home/bob/desktop/shortcut_to_minesweepe: You have no new high scores. You have never had a high score.

hints: Strings that end in '=' and look like keyboard soup are often base64.
Bob's encryption notes literally tell you the decoding command.
Try: cat definitely_not_a_secret.txt | base64 -d   (or copy the line: base64 -d <text>)
completion: Bob has been informed that base64 is an encoding, not encryption.
He has responded by base64-encoding it twice.
